# JusPrin Cloud coins: implementation plan (working doc, 2026-11-01)

Untracked working document. It turns the pricing plan Kenneth settled on 2026-11-01 into concrete work on the three codebases involved: the gateway in `tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), the Obico server it is built on (`obico-server`, where the v1 credit table lives), and the desktop app (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and the Agent page under `AgentUI/`). Companion docs: `pricing-mental-model-2026-10.md`, `journey-cost-2026-10.md`, `obico-pro-pricing-data-2026-10.md`, `v1-pricing-data-2026-10.md`.

Every "recommend" below is my opinion; every "decided" is Kenneth's. Code facts were read from the checkouts on 2026-11-01 (tsd-enterprise master, JusPrin `jusprin-newui` at 69780c7af4, ops master).

## 1. The plan being implemented

- The unit is a **coin**, about 2 cents. Coins pay per message, not per token. A **basic** message (DeepSeek V4 Flash class) costs 1 coin; an **expert** message (Claude Sonnet 5.5 class, not Opus) costs 5 coins. The 1:5 ratio is decided.
- **Pack:** 500 coins for $10, never expire. Optional auto-reload at a discount.
- **$10/month:** 750 coins, basic messages cost coins, unused coins lost at the end of each month.
- **$20/month:** 1,000 coins plus unlimited basic messages, unused coins lost each month. Needs fair-use wording.
- **Obico subscribers:** 20% off both subscriptions.
- **Sign-up grant:** about $10 of coins (500), expiring after one month. **Trickle:** a free monthly basic allowance for light users.
- **Rewards:** coins of real value for a print report with a photo and detailed text, with a human review flag for bad ones.
- **Launch period:** discounted, not free, coins.
- **Alert:** tell the person when their usage has grown to where a subscription saves them money.
- **BYOK** (the person's own API key) stays free with no sign-in.

### The cost figures the margins rest on

Measured per user message, one run per journey, from `journey-cost-2026-10.md` (Sonnet added 2026-11-01, so the peer session's "Sonnet still unmeasured" is out of date):

| Tier | Model | Cost per user message | Price at 2¢ a coin | Gross margin |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Basic | DeepSeek V4 Flash (OpenRouter) | 0.4¢ to 1¢; 5¢ when the agent polled the slicer 75 times | 2¢ (1 coin) | 50% to 80%; negative in the polling case |
| Expert | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 5.6¢ to 7.4¢, mean 6.3¢ over 14 messages | 10¢ (5 coins) | 26% to 44%, 37% at the mean |
| (not offered) | Claude Opus 5.5 | 10¢ to 21¢ | 10¢ | negative |

"Per user message" divides a whole session's cost, including the turns the app starts by itself (file opened, slice finished), by the messages the person typed. So the margins above already assume app-started turns are not charged (see section 3.3). Two cost prerequisites move these: Anthropic's 5-minute cache expiry during a slow slice rewrote 72k tokens for $0.36 on Opus (section 7.1), and the slicer polling tripled one basic session (section 7.2).

## 2. What exists today

**Gateway.** `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` is a raw ASGI endpoint on daphne (`tsdws-prod`) that streams `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/messages` (Anthropic format) and `/responses` (OpenAI format) to an upstream model. `credits.py` admits each turn: a Redis rate limit of 60 turns a minute per person (`JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE`), then one v1 credit per turn through `consume_credit_for_pipeline` in `obico-server/backend/app/jusprin/ai_credits.py`, which decrements `JusPrinAICredit.ai_credit_used_current_month` against `ai_credit_free_monthly_quota` (50 a month, -1 for unlimited). A turn is every request that carries the same `X-JusPrin-Turn` header; title requests (`X-JusPrin-Request: title`) are free. The Redis keys `seen` and `charged` make the charge idempotent per turn for an hour. Exhaustion is a 402 with code `quota_exhausted`.

**Aliases.** `aliases.py` reads `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` (a ConfigMap, `ops/tsd/prod/jusprin-v2-gateway.yaml`). Production has one alias, `slicer-1`, label "Slicer 1", efforts fast/thorough, Anthropic backend `claude-sonnet-5-5` at 100%, OpenAI backend `gpt-6.1-sol` at 0%. Only the formats `anthropic` and `responses` exist. There is no DeepSeek backend and no image stripping.

**Account.** `GET /jusprin/api/me/` (obico-server `JusPrinMeViewSet`) answers `{"user": {...}, "ai_credits": {...}}`; the desktop app reads only the email (`CloudAccount.cpp:233`). `GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models` lists aliases with `format`, `efforts`, `default_effort`.

**Billing.** Chargebee, site `obico`. v1 sells `jusprin-unlimited-monthly` ($6.99) and `jusprin-unlimited-annual` ($59.99) through `web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py`: hosted checkout pages, a callback, a webhook that upserts `JusPrinPlan` and flips the v1 quota to -1. An Obico Pro discount coupon (30%) is applied at checkout after a live Chargebee status call. Obico's own code (`web_ent/app_ent/cb_views.py`, `detective_hour_accounting.py`) already has the two patterns the coin ledger needs: one-time packs sold as a non-recurring add-on on a placeholder subscription (`pre-paid-detective-hour-pack`, credited from the `invoice_generated` webhook, keyed `inv:<invoice id>`), and per-term included credits keyed `sub:<resource_version>:<suffix>` so a repeated webhook never double-credits. `DetectiveHourTransaction` is a ledger of signed amounts with a `forfeitable` flag; balance is a sum.

**Obico subscriber check.** `app_ent.models.Subscription.active()` on `user.subscription`, mirrored to `user.is_pro`. Local, no Chargebee call needed.

**Rewards precedent.** `credit_dh_for_contribution` (a Celery task) grants non-forfeitable detection hours for labelling print frames; `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` is the per-label human review flag set in the admin.

**Desktop app.** `ProviderProfile.hpp` row `jusprin` (default model `slicer-1`, `account_sign_in` true) makes `ProviderAgent` send `X-JusPrin-Turn`, `X-JusPrin-Request` (reply or title) and `X-JusPrin-Chat`. `ProviderAgent::http_error` maps 402 to `quota_exhausted` with the text "Your JusPrin account has used its Agent allowance for now. See your account for more." The Agent page gets `model_catalog` (per provider: models with `efforts`), `chat_model`, `account_status` (sign-in phase only) and `setup_keys` (the signed-in email). `ModelPickers.tsx` draws the per-chat model and effort pickers; `Preferences.tsx` has an `account` section. Print records (`ManufacturingHistory.hpp`, `GcodeRecord` with destinations and prints) live in the project file; nothing about them reaches the server.

**Cache control.** `AnthropicCodec.cpp` sets `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}` with no `ttl` on the last tool, the system text and the last user message. The append-only chat record (commit 1635438d4f) already makes the slice-finished turn read the whole prior prompt from cache, so only expiry during a pause remains.

**Slice polling.** `slice_start`'s result note already tells the model "Checking on it from this turn shows nothing the person can't already see" (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2155`). DeepSeek polled `workspace_inspect` anyway, 75 times in one run and twice in another.

## 3. Gateway: the coin ledger

New module `web_ent/jusprin/coins/` (models, ledger, webhooks, tests), replacing the `consume_credit_for_pipeline` call in `credits.py` for v2 only. v1 keeps `JusPrinAICredit` untouched; the v1 app never reaches these paths.

### 3.1 Tables

```
CoinGrant            one lot of coins
  user, kind {pack, subscription, signup, trickle, reward, launch_bonus, adjustment}
  coins_granted, coins_remaining
  expires_at          null = never (packs, rewards)
  basic_only          bool (trickle lots pay basic turns only)
  source_ref          unique per user: inv:<invoice>, sub:<resource_version>:coins,
                      signup, trickle:<yyyy-mm>, report:<print report id>
  created_at

CoinCharge           one per charged turn
  user, turn_id      unique together
  alias, tier {basic, expert}, coins (0 for a turn covered by unlimited basic or a free app turn)
  origin {person, app}
  created_at         indexed with user

CoinAllocation       which lots paid a charge (for refunds and the balance breakdown)
  charge, grant, coins
```

`JusPrinPlan` (already there, one row per user) becomes the v2 subscription record too: add `current_term_start`, `current_term_end`, `external_resource_version` as Obico's `Subscription` has, and treat `plan_id` prefixes `jusprin-coins-` as v2 plans. v1's `jusprin-unlimited-` plans stay recognised.

### 3.2 Charging a turn

`ledger.charge_turn(user_id, turn_id, alias, origin)`, called from `credits.admit` in place of the v1 call, inside `transaction.atomic()` with `select_for_update()` on the person's live lots:

1. Cost = the alias's `coins` (section 3.4). Origin `app` costs 0 (section 3.3). Tier basic on an active $20 plan costs 0 until the fair-use ceiling (section 6), then 1.
2. Lazy trickle: if no `trickle:<this month>` lot exists for the person, create it first (section 3.5). This replaces a monthly sweep over 250k accounts.
3. Draw order: lots that expire soonest first, never-expiring lots last. Among lots with the same expiry, oldest first. `basic_only` lots are skipped for expert turns. So a sign-up lot (30 days) is spent before a subscription lot (term end), and both before a pack.
4. Not enough coins: raise so `admit` returns a new `Admission.COINS_EXHAUSTED`, which the gateway answers as 402 with code `coins_exhausted` and a body the client can act on: `{"balance": 3, "cost": 5, "affordable_aliases": ["slicer-basic"], "plan": null}`. `errors.py` grows that entry; the old `quota_exhausted` text stays for v1.
5. Record `CoinCharge` and its allocations. The Redis `charged` key stays as the fast path; the unique `(user, turn_id)` is the truth, so a retried first request of a turn never pays twice.

Only the first request of a turn charges, as today, so tool-call follow-ups inside a turn are free however many there are. This is what makes "per message" honest and also why the polling fix matters: follow-ups cost the gateway real money while charging nothing.

### 3.3 Which turns are charged (recommend)

Charge only turns the person started. The app also starts turns by itself: the file-opened report, the slice-finished note, print-issue and setup-changed skills. Those are the agent doing its job unasked, and the measured per-message costs already include them, so they fit the margin table at 0 coins. The client tells the gateway with a third value of the existing header, `X-JusPrin-Request: note`, set by `ProviderAgent` from a new `turn_origin` on the transcript (the host knows which message id started the turn: `start_turn(note.id)` in `AgentHost.cpp:1836` versus a person's message).

Guard: the Redis minute limit already caps 60 turns a minute. Add a daily counter of free app turns per person (Redis, 24 h) and charge them as basic past 50 a day. That is high enough that no real session hits it and low enough to stop a script.

### 3.4 Tiers in the alias config

`aliases.py` gains two required keys per alias, `tier` ("basic" or "expert") and `coins` (integer), and one optional backend key, `images` (default true). `GET /models` reports `tier` and `coins` so the client can print "5 coins a message" next to the model name without hard-coding prices anywhere.

Production aliases (recommend):

| id | label | tier | coins | backend |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| `slicer-1` | Expert | expert | 5 | Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` (unchanged, so every existing chat pinned to it keeps working) |
| `slicer-basic` | Basic | basic | 1 | OpenRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` in the `responses` format, `images: false` |

Keeping the id `slicer-1` avoids an `unknown_model` for chats that already exist; only its label changes. The client's default model is the `ProviderProfile` row's `slicer-1`, so new chats default to Expert. Whether a new chat should default to Expert or Basic is a product decision; I recommend Expert while the person has coins, because the sign-up grant is meant to show the best version, and the picker makes Basic one click away.

DeepSeek work the gateway needs: `upstream.py`'s `prepare()` strips image blocks from a request when the chosen backend has `images: false` (the measurement proxy did this; the model's hosts reject image input), and leaves a text note in their place so the model knows a picture was dropped. OpenRouter speaks the Responses API, so no new wire format is needed. First-party DeepSeek is cheaper per cached token but speaks chat-completions and serves a different model under the same name; not for launch.

### 3.5 Lots that are not bought

- **Sign-up grant** (decided: about $10, one month): 500 coins, `expires_at = now + 30 days`, `source_ref = signup`, created on the person's first v2 request or first `/models` call when they have no lot at all. One per account, ever. No device checks; Obico sign-up already requires a verified email, and a second account to farm another $5 of model cost is not worth defending against now.
- **Trickle** (decided in principle; size to choose): 50 coins a month, `basic_only`, expiring at the end of the calendar month, created lazily (3.2 step 2). v1's free users had a median of 2 chats a month and a 90th percentile of 6, so 50 basic messages covers nearly every light user and costs at most about 50¢ a month each. Recommend 50; 30 is defensible.
- **Rewards**: section 8.
- **Launch bonus** (decided: discounted, never free): recommend doubling the coins of every pack bought before a date in a setting, `JUSPRIN_LAUNCH_DOUBLE_UNTIL`, as a second lot `kind = launch_bonus` on the same invoice ref. It needs no Chargebee change and works the same for any payment method added later. A Chargebee coupon on the pack is the alternative if Kenneth prefers the discount to show on the receipt.

### 3.6 Expiry

Expiry is a comparison at read and charge time (`expires_at > now`), never a sweep, so a lot simply stops counting. A nightly task zeroes `coins_remaining` on expired lots and writes the forfeited count into Langfuse or a metric, which is the "how much of their quota do subscribers use" number Kenneth expects to be under half.

## 4. Billing: Chargebee

Reuse the two patterns Obico already runs.

- **Packs:** plan `jusprin-coin-pack` ($0 placeholder subscription, like `pre-paid-detective-hour-pack`) with non-recurring add-on `jusprin-500-coins` at $10. `generate_coin_pack_checkout_url` copies `generate_prepaid_dhpack_checkout_url`. The `invoice_generated` webhook (status paid) creates `CoinGrant(kind=pack, source_ref=inv:<id>)`. The placeholder row that remembers the Chargebee subscription id can be a `JusPrinCoinPackPlaceholder` or a field on `JusPrinPlan`; the field is simpler.
- **Subscriptions:** plans `jusprin-coins-10-monthly` ($10, 750 coins) and `jusprin-coins-20-monthly` ($20, 1,000 coins, unlimited basic). The existing `jusprin_cb_webhook` is extended: on `subscription_activated`, `subscription_renewed` and `subscription_changed` with status active, `CoinGrant(kind=subscription, coins=<plan's>, expires_at=current_term_end, source_ref=sub:<resource_version>:coins)` via `get_or_create`, and the `JusPrinPlan` term fields are updated. On `cancelled`, `expired_at = now`; the current lot keeps its term-end expiry so a person who cancels mid-month keeps what they paid for. No proration on plan change: the old lot expires at its own term end, the new lot is granted in full. Simpler than Obico's prorated reversal and errs in the person's favour.
- **Obico discount** (decided: 20%): a Chargebee coupon with `duration_type = forever`, applied at checkout when `user.subscription.active()` is true locally (no live Chargebee retrieve; the v1 code's try/except around one is exactly the kind of swallowed error AGENTS.md forbids). When Obico's `upsert_subscription` handles a cancellation, it removes the coupon from any active `jusprin-coins-` subscription of that person with `Subscription.remove_coupons`. Annual JusPrin plans are not in the decided plan; if added later, the same code path works.
- **Auto-reload with a discount** (decided, optional for the person): a flag on `JusPrinPlan` (`auto_reload`), set from the account page after a first pack purchase so a payment source exists. A Celery task, queued by `charge_turn` when the never-expiring balance drops below 50 coins and the flag is on, creates a Chargebee invoice for add-on `jusprin-500-coins-reload` at $9 (10% off) with `Invoice.create_for_charge_items_and_charges` or the site's equivalent, charged immediately; the `invoice_generated` webhook then grants the lot like any pack. Never charge inside a chat request. A failed payment turns the flag off and tells the person on the account page.
- **Pricing page:** `web_ent/frontend/src/views/jusprin/JusPrinPricingPage.vue` is rewritten around coins, the two plans, the pack, the fair-use text (section 6) and the Obico discount. Purchases happen in the browser on Chargebee hosted pages; the desktop app opens the page, it does not embed checkout.
- **Portal:** `generate_jusprin_portal_session` already exists for the Chargebee customer portal (cancel, card changes).
- **Brazil:** 10 of v1's 34 payers paid with Brazilian cards and 10 of 15 failed renewals were Brazilian. Whether Chargebee on this site can take Pix, and at what BRL price, is to verify before launch, not assumed. The one-time pack is the product that fits a Pix buyer (Pix is one-time in most stores), which is another reason the pack exists.
- **v1 subscribers:** people on `jusprin-unlimited-*` who sign in to v2 are treated as the $20 plan until their current term ends (a lot of 1,000 coins per term plus unlimited basic, keyed to the resource version like any subscription), then they choose. Their v1 app is unaffected.

## 5. Account endpoint and balance display

### 5.1 `GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account`

New Django view (plain request handling, on `tsdweb-prod`, next to `/models`), bearer-authenticated like `/models`:

```json
{
  "coins": {"total": 612, "lots": [
      {"kind": "signup", "coins": 112, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
      {"kind": "trickle", "coins": 50, "basic_only": true, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
      {"kind": "pack", "coins": 450, "expires_at": null}]},
  "plan": {"id": "jusprin-coins-20-monthly", "renews_at": "...", "unlimited_basic": true,
           "basic_used_this_term": 212, "basic_fair_use": 600, "obico_discount": true,
           "auto_reload": false},
  "prices": {"coin_cents": 2, "pack": {"coins": 500, "cents": 1000},
             "plans": [{"id": "...", "cents": 1000, "coins": 750}, {"id": "...", "cents": 2000, "coins": 1000, "unlimited_basic": true}]},
  "usage_30d": {"basic_turns": 140, "expert_turns": 60, "coins": 440},
  "suggestion": {"plan": "jusprin-coins-10-monthly", "saves_cents_per_month": 380}
}
```

`/jusprin/api/me/` stays as the sign-in check; the app calls `/account` after a sign-in check, after every completed or failed turn on the `jusprin` provider (one small GET, no streaming change), when the Preferences account section opens, and when the window regains focus after the person was sent to the browser to buy. A cheaper later step is a `X-JusPrin-Coins` response header on the stream start, but `AgentTransport` does not surface response headers today, so the GET comes first.

### 5.2 In the app

- **Model picker** (`ModelPickers.tsx`): each option shows its price from `ModelOptionInfo.coins`, "Expert · 5 coins" and "Basic · 1 coin". An option the balance cannot afford is drawn but marked, and the chat's model falls to the affordable one with a one-line note in the composer, not a silent switch.
- **Balance** (new `AccountStatusPayload` fields or a new `account` host message with the JSON above): a coin count in the composer's provider row, "612 coins", with a hover or tap breakdown "112 expire 1 Dec, 50 basic-only, 450 never expire". The same breakdown, the plan, usage and the buy and subscribe buttons live in Preferences › Account.
- **Exhaustion:** the 402 body drives the failed-message card: "This message needs 5 coins; you have 3." with buttons "Switch this chat to Basic" (when `affordable_aliases` is non-empty), "Buy 500 coins ($10)" and "Subscribe" (open the pricing page in the browser). `ProviderAgent::http_error` passes the body through instead of its fixed text when the code is `coins_exhausted`.
- **BYOK unchanged:** none of this appears for providers with an API key.
- **Design:** every colour, size and radius through the token file and `ShellTheme` or CSS variables per `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`; the chip and card get boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas before code.

### 5.3 The "subscription would save you money" alert (decided)

Computed server-side in `/account` from the last 30 days of `CoinCharge`:

- cost at pack price = coins × 2¢;
- cost on the $10 plan = $10 + max(0, coins − 750) × 2¢;
- cost on the $20 plan = $20 + max(0, expert coins − 1,000) × 2¢ (basic turns free up to fair use);
- apply the 20% Obico discount when it applies;
- `suggestion` names the cheapest plan when it saves at least $3 a month against what the person is doing now (pack, or current plan).

The app shows it once as a dismissable line above the composer and in Preferences › Account, re-evaluated when the 30-day window changes the answer. Preferences › Account has the switch "Alert me when a subscription would save me money", on by default (the message is in the person's favour; the switch exists so it can be silenced). The caveat from the brainstorm stands: this recruits exactly the heavy users, which is why the plans give 1.5× and not 2× the pack rate.

## 6. Fair use for unlimited basic

Numbers: a basic message cost 0.4¢ to 1¢ normally and 5¢ when the agent polled the slicer, so the $20 plan loses money past 400 to 2,000 basic messages a month after its 1,000 coins of expert are also used. Rule (recommend):

- **Ceiling:** 600 basic messages a month at no coins. Past it, a basic message costs 1 coin from the balance like on the $10 plan. 600 is 20 a day, above anything the measured sessions or v1's heaviest payer (130 chats in a month) suggest a person does by hand, and it caps the worst case at about $6 to $30 of cost on $20 of revenue.
- **Rate:** the existing 60 turns a minute, plus the 50 free app turns a day (3.3).
- **Automation:** the page says the plan is for a person using JusPrin, not for scripts or shared accounts; the ledger gives the numbers to act on, and acting is a human step through the admin, not a detector.
- **Page wording:** "Unlimited basic messages for one person using JusPrin by hand; after 600 in a month, basic messages cost 1 coin each. Expert messages always cost 5 coins." Say the number. Every surveyed vendor hides it and gets the anger at the boundary (mental model doc, question 2); the measured usage says 600 is a boundary almost nobody reaches, so saying it costs nothing.

The polling fix (7.2) is what makes the 5¢ case go away; until it ships, the ceiling is the only protection.

## 7. The two cost prerequisites

### 7.1 Anthropic cache lifetime

Fact: Sonnet 5.5 cache writes cost $2.50 per million tokens for the 5-minute lifetime and $4 for one hour (fetched 2026-11-01). A session wrote 40k to 80k tokens in all, so the 1-hour lifetime adds $0.06 to $0.12 per session; one expiry after a pause over 5 minutes rewrote 42k to 72k tokens, $0.10 to $0.18 at Sonnet rates. So the 1-hour lifetime pays for itself at one real pause per session, and a person who slices, waits, reads and types pauses more than that.

Where (recommend): the gateway, not the app. `upstream.py`'s `prepare()` already parses the Anthropic body; it adds `"ttl": "1h"` to every `cache_control` block for the `anthropic` backend. That keeps the pricing lever on the server, ships without an app release, and BYOK users keep paying Anthropic's default on their own key. Anthropic requires 1-hour breakpoints to come before 5-minute ones in the prompt; setting all three to 1h satisfies that. Verify on the live gateway by comparing `cache_creation_input_tokens` across a turn separated by a 10-minute pause, before and after.

The slice-finished turn itself no longer rewrites the prefix since the append-only record landed (commit 1635438d4f); the 1-hour lifetime covers the slice taking longer than 5 minutes.

### 7.2 Stop the agent polling the slicer

Two steps, the small one first:

1. **Guard in the host** (`ToolExecutionCoordinator`): while a slice the agent started in this turn is running, a `workspace_inspect` that asks for `slicing`, or a `slice_report`, is answered with the tool error code `busy` and the message "The slice is still running. This turn has nothing left to do: the app starts a new turn with the outcome. Finish your reply." After the third such refusal in one turn the host ends the turn (the same path as the person's Stop) and the slice-finished note turn carries on. `busy` is in the one error-code list (`Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`), and a waiting slice is an expected state, so this is normal control flow, not a swallowed error. Each refused call still costs one small request, so three is the cap on the waste.
2. **End the turn at `slice_start`** (the real fix, later): when `slice_start` returns `started: true`, the host closes the turn instead of returning the result to the model, and the slice-finished note turn carries both the `tool_result` for that call and the note text in one user message. The model never gets a chance to poll, the person sees the model's text before the tool plus the slice card, and the follow-up request happens once. This touches `ProviderAgent`'s turn continuation and both codecs (a deferred tool result), so it is its own piece of work with the tool-pairing rules of both wire formats tested.

The measured waste was two thirds of a basic session's cost on a debug build; a shipped build slices faster so the poll count is lower, but the fix removes the behaviour rather than the opportunity.

## 8. Rewards for print reports

Decided: coins of meaningful value for a photo plus detailed text; this audience did not game Obico's labelling rewards; keep a human review flag.

- **Where the button lives:** the G-code marker in the chat (`GcodeMarker.tsx`, drawn for each export or send from `GcodeRecord`) and the print history list get "Report how it printed". The form takes one or more photos, a required text of at least 200 characters, and an outcome choice (good, flawed, failed). The record's facts go along automatically: G-code hash, printer, material, process, slice statistics, the plate's manufacturing input hash and, when the person agrees, the project's setup diff from the checkpoint.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/print_reports` (multipart, bearer token, plain Django on `tsdweb`). Stores a `PrintReport` row and the photos in the object store the way `UploadedTimelapse` stores videos. One report per `(user, gcode_hash)`; at most three rewarded reports a day per person.
- **Reward:** 25 coins (50¢ at pack price, half an expert session) as `CoinGrant(kind=reward, source_ref=report:<id>)`, never expiring, granted at once when the automatic checks pass (photo present and decodable, text length, not a duplicate). The app shows "+25 coins" in the balance.
- **Review:** `PrintReportReview(report, invalid, note)` with an admin page like `EntPrintShotFeedbackAdmin`, filterable by unreviewed. Marking one invalid writes a `-25` `adjustment` lot (balance can go to zero, not below, for the rest) and after two invalid reports the person's reports stop earning. The invalid share is the number to watch; Obico's `PrintShotFeedbackReview.invalid` share can be counted now for a baseline (offered earlier, not yet done).
- **Why not in the gateway stream:** reports are not chats; they are the training-data channel, so they get their own table and their own retention rule.

## 9. Sign-in, accounts and the v1 free quota

- The sign-up lot is created on first contact (3.5), so no change to the OAuth flow.
- v1's `JusPrinAICredit` keeps serving the v1 app. The v2 gateway stops calling `consume_credit_for_pipeline`; its `quota_exhausted` code stays in `errors.py` for v1 compatibility but is no longer raised by v2.
- Account deletion: `can_account_be_deleted` in `app_ent.models` blocks deletion while a prepaid detection-hour pack exists; coin lots should not block deletion (unused coins are forfeited, said on the page).

## 10. Measuring it

- `_Turn._log` already writes one Langfuse generation per request with token usage; add `coins`, `tier`, `origin` and `charge_id` to its metadata so cost per coin is one query.
- A nightly Celery task computes, per tier, upstream cost (from captured `usage` and the price table) against coins charged for the day, and the share of subscription coins forfeited. These are hypotheses 1 to 3 of the mental model measured on real people instead of on four harness runs.
- Alerts: margin per tier below 20% for three days; free app turns per person above the daily cap; reward invalid share above 10%.

## 11. Order of work and tests

1. **Ledger and charging** (gateway + obico-server migration): tables, `charge_turn`, draw order, lazy trickle, sign-up lot, `coins_exhausted` 402 body, `tier`/`coins`/`images` in aliases, `slicer-basic` alias with image stripping, `/account`. Tests in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/`: draw order (expiring first, basic-only skipped for expert, never-expiring last), idempotent charge on a retried first request, two concurrent first requests of different turns against one lot (`select_for_update`), expiry at the boundary, free app turns and their daily cap, the 402 body, image stripping only for `images: false`, and a `/models` response carrying prices. Gateway test harness pattern: `test_gateway.py` with the MockTransport injection the file already uses.
2. **App:** `X-JusPrin-Request: note`, `coins` in `ModelOptionInfo` and the pickers, the `/account` fetch and balance chip, the exhaustion card with its three actions, Preferences › Account. Vitest for the page (`ModelPickers.test.tsx`, a new `Account.test.tsx`), Catch2 for `ProviderAgent`'s header and 402 handling, one live end-to-end run through the shell harness against staging (`app-stg.obico.io` runs the same image) at a stated spend.
3. **Chargebee:** plans, add-ons, coupon, checkout views, webhook branches, pricing page, v1-subscriber carry-over. Tests with recorded webhook payloads, including a repeated `subscription_renewed` (no double lot), a cancellation mid-term (lot keeps its expiry), an `invoice_generated` for the pack, and the Obico-cancel coupon removal. Staging run with Chargebee's test site before production.
4. **Cost prerequisites:** 1-hour ttl in `prepare()` (test: the body sent upstream carries `ttl` on every `cache_control`; live check of cache write counts across a 10-minute pause), then the polling guard (host test: third refused poll ends the turn; the slice-finished note turn still runs).
5. **Rewards:** endpoint, storage, admin, app form and button. Tests: duplicate hash rejected, text too short rejected, daily cap, invalid review claws back once.
6. **Alert and auto-reload and launch bonus:** suggestion maths with unit tests on the four cases (pack cheaper, $10 cheaper, $20 cheaper, Obico discount flips the answer); auto-reload task with a failed payment path; `JUSPRIN_LAUNCH_DOUBLE_UNTIL`.

Steps 1, 3 and 4 touch `tsd-enterprise` and `ops` (the ConfigMap gains the second alias and the OpenRouter key env; both deployments restart). Step 2 touches the app. Steps 1 and 2 can be built in parallel once the `/account` shape and the 402 body are agreed, which this document is for.

## 12. Decisions still Kenneth's

Each with my recommendation; none blocks step 1's tables.

1. **Default tier for a new chat:** Expert (recommend) or Basic.
2. **Alias ids:** keep `slicer-1` as Expert and add `slicer-basic` (recommend), or rename both.
3. **App-started turns free** with a 50-a-day cap (recommend) or charged like a person's message.
4. **Trickle size:** 50 basic-only coins a month (recommend) or 30.
5. **Fair-use ceiling on the $20 plan:** 600 basic messages a month, stated on the page (recommend).
6. **Reward size:** 25 coins per accepted report, three a day (recommend); 10 to 20 was the range in the draft.
7. **Launch discount form:** double coins on packs by server flag (recommend) or a Chargebee coupon.
8. **v1 unlimited subscribers:** treated as the $20 plan until term end (recommend).
9. **Pix and BRL pricing:** verify Chargebee's support on this site before promising it.
10. **Domain:** still open from the gateway rollout; the pricing page URL the app opens moves with it.

# Where a person meets the coins, and how each point should feel (working doc, 2026-11-01)

Untracked design notes, written before any coin UI is drawn or built. The pricing plan is in `pricing-implementation-plan-2026-11.md`; this document is about the person, not the ledger. It lists every point in the product where someone meets coins, says what goes wrong there in other products, and gives one opinion per point. Boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas come after Kenneth has reacted to these.

What the survey of other products (`pricing-case-studies-2026-10.md`) says goes wrong, in one list: people cannot picture what an abstract credit buys; two kinds of credit with different expiry rules confuse everyone; the anger is at the boundary, when something they were doing stops; a balance that drops for reasons they did not cause breeds distrust; "unlimited" with an unstated ceiling is read as a lie once reached.

## Five rules that apply at every point

1. **One word, one unit.** "Coins", never "credits", never tokens. A coin is explained once, in messages: "an Expert message is 5 coins, a Basic message is 1". Dollars appear only on the page where money changes hands.
2. **Coins only move when the person sends a message.** Turns the app starts (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) are free, and the balance never changes without a message from the person. That one fact is what makes the balance trustworthy; it is stated on the plan page in one sentence: "Only messages you send cost coins."
3. **Expiring coins are named by what they are, with a date. Bought coins are just "coins" and never expire.** "112 welcome coins, until 1 Dec." "50 free Basic messages this month." "450 coins." Never a bare number that mixes them. The draw rule is stated once, in the balance breakdown: "Expiring coins are used first."
4. **Say the number before the boundary, not at it.** Every ceiling (balance, fair use, expiry) is shown on the way there with a count, so reaching it is never news.
5. **Nothing typed is lost and nothing stops silently.** A message that cannot be sent stays in the composer with a way to send it anyway.

## The points, in the order a person meets them

### 1. First launch: own key or JusPrin account

Where: the Agent setup in Preferences › Agent (the one setup flow, decided 2026-10-23) and the welcome screen.

Today the choice is "your own API key" against "sign in to JusPrin", and nothing says what signing in gives. Opinion: the JusPrin row says, in one line, "Free to start: 500 coins for your first month, about 100 Expert or 500 Basic messages. Your own key stays free." No dollar figure. The first month's grant is the whole pitch at this point, so it is the one number on the screen.

### 2. Picking Basic or Expert for a chat

Where: the model picker in the composer (`ModelPickers.tsx`), per chat.

Risk: "Expert, 5 coins" against "Basic, 1 coin" tells the price but not the trade. Opinion: each option gets the price and one plain clause about when to use it: "Basic · 1 coin · setting up an ordinary print" and "Expert · 5 coins · troubleshooting, tricky models, anything you'd ask a person". No model names, no vendor names: the person is choosing how much help to buy, not which company's model. The chosen tier shows on the composer as a small label, so the price of the next message is always visible before sending.

Default for a new chat: Expert while the welcome coins last, because the first weeks decide whether the person stays. After that, the last tier the person chose.

Where: the composer's provider row, and Preferences › Account.

Risk: a meter that visibly ticks down per message makes people ration and resent (Meshy, Suno); a hidden one feels like a trick when it runs out. Opinion: show the number quietly and constantly, "612 coins", with no animation and no per-message decrement flash. Hovering or tapping it opens the breakdown by kind and date (rule 3). The number changes only when the person sends a message (rule 2), so a person who watches it learns it is honest.

Preferences › Account carries the same breakdown plus a short activity list: date, chat name, tier, coins. "Where did my coins go" has an answer the person can look up alone.

### 4. Coins that will expire

Where: the balance breakdown, Preferences › Account, and one notice.

Welcome coins expire after 30 days, subscription coins at month end, the free Basic allowance at month end. Opinion: the breakdown always shows the date beside each expiring lot. One notice, seven days before a lot expires, inside the composer area once: "388 welcome coins expire on 1 Dec." Never an email for this. When the lot has expired, nothing says "you lost 388 coins"; the breakdown simply shows what remains. Losing something you did not pay for should not be dramatised.

### 5. The next message costs more than the person has

Where: the composer, before sending; the failed-message card if the gateway refuses anyway.

This is the boundary where every surveyed product earns its anger. Opinion: catch it before sending. The app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next Expert message cannot be paid, the Send button becomes "Send with Basic (1 coin)" and a one-line note says why: "You have 3 coins; Expert needs 5." The typed text is untouched. "Buy coins" and "Subscribe" sit next to it, not instead of it. Only a race between two sends reaches the gateway's 402, and the failed card then does the same three things with the text kept in the composer.

Earlier than that: when the balance falls below one session's worth of the chat's tier (about 25 coins for Expert), the composer says once "About 5 Expert messages left", so the boundary is expected, not met.

### 6. Unlimited Basic and its ceiling

Where: the plan page, Preferences › Account, one notice in the composer.

Risk: "unlimited" that stops at 600 reads as a lie. Opinion: never write "unlimited" alone. The plan page says "Unlimited Basic messages for one person using JusPrin by hand, up to 600 a month; after that, 1 coin each." Preferences › Account shows "412 of 600 free Basic messages this month". At 500, one notice. At 600, the composer's tier label changes to "Basic · 1 coin" with one line saying why. Nobody measured reaches 600, so this costs nothing and removes the asterisk.

### 7. Subscription coins the person did not use

Where: Preferences › Account; one notice; the suggestion line.

Kenneth expects most subscribers to use under half their coins. Opinion: tell them. The month-end notice is the same as point 4 ("240 coins expire on 30 Nov"). And the "a subscription would save you money" alert runs in both directions: when a subscriber has forfeited more than half their coins two months running, the suggestion says "You used 310 coins a month lately; a 500-coin pack for $10 would last you longer." The alert itself (pack to subscription) appears once above the composer, dismissable, with the saving in dollars and the arithmetic one tap away ("You spent 820 coins in the last 30 days: $16.40 in packs, $10 on the monthly plan"). It is on by default and has a switch in Preferences › Account.

Where: the pricing page in the browser (Chargebee hosted checkout), then back in the app.

Risk: the bounce to a browser, and the silence when the person returns ("did it go through?"). Opinion: the page has three cards and each states its expiry rule in its own words: "500 coins, $10, never expire"; "750 coins a month, $10, reset each month"; "1,000 coins a month plus unlimited Basic (up to 600), $20, reset each month". Launch double-coins shows on the pack card with its end date.

Back in the app: the balance refreshes when the window regains focus, and the composer shows one line, "+500 coins", so the person knows it worked without opening Preferences.

### 9. When the welcome month ends

Where: the first launch after day 30.

Risk: the person comes back to zero and reads it as "the free trial is over, pay up", the moment Obico's data says people leave. Opinion: the composer shows what they have, not what they lost: "50 free Basic messages this month" with the tier set to Basic. Expert is one click away and shows its price. No wall, no modal, no "upgrade" word.

### 10. Rewards for a print report

Where: the G-code marker in the chat and the print history, after a print.

Opinion: show the reward before the work, in the button itself: "Tell us how it printed · 25 coins". The form says what earns it: a photo of the printed object and a few sentences. The coins land at once with a "+25 coins" line in the composer. If a report is later marked invalid, the clawback is visible in the Account activity list with a one-line reason, never a silent drop. Where: the model picker, which lists every provider the person set up.

Opinion: coins and prices appear only on the JusPrin provider's entries. A person with both an own key and an account sees "OpenAI · gpt-5.4-mini" without a price and "JusPrin · Expert · 5 coins" with one. Nothing about coins appears anywhere for a person who never signs in.

Where: the pricing page and Preferences › Account.

Opinion: one line, "Obico member: 20% off subscriptions", shown as the price on the card and as a note in Account. It is detected, never claimed or entered.

Three boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas, in this order, because they carry the most risk: the composer with the tier label, balance and the pre-send "Send with Basic" state (points 2, 3, 5); Preferences › Account with the breakdown, the fair-use count and the activity list (points 3, 4, 6, 7); the pricing page's three cards (point 8). Both precedents checked. GitHub Copilot named its unit after the expensive thing, "premium requests", gave each model a multiplier up to 20×, and has since moved to "AI credits" with usage-based billing, so the multiplier scheme is now its legacy system. Lovable started with "messages" at one credit per message, switched to complexity-weighted credits in 2025, and in 2026 split chat back out to a per-message price with a daily allowance. Both found that one abstract unit across tiers was the thing people kept not understanding. That shapes my answer.

**The unit.** My real opinion is that the most intuitive unit is the Expert message itself, and the abstraction only exists to charge for Basic. Basic costs under a cent a message, so I would stop charging for it: Basic is free for everyone within the 600-a-month fair use, and the only thing anyone counts or buys is Expert messages. "100 Expert messages for $10" needs no explanation, no conversion line, no two kinds of balance. The cost is a free Basic user at worst about $4 to $6 a month, at measured typical use a few cents, which fits your stated willingness to subsidise model cost for traction. Your 1:5 ratio survives as the price gap between a free message and a 10-cent one. It also deletes half the ledger: no basic-only lots, no tier multiplier, no "which coins paid for this".

If Basic stays paid, the word is **credits**, not coins. Coins say "game economy"; credits already mean "a prepaid balance you spend" to everyone, which is exactly what the pack is, and every surveyed product that tried another word ended up at credits anyway. The mapping line travels with the word wherever it first appears: "1 credit is a Basic message; an Expert message is 5." The balance is then always shown translated, "612 credits: 612 Basic or 122 Expert", because the number alone is what people cannot picture.

**The plans.** Avoid Pro, Plus and Premium: they say rank, not content, and Obico Pro already exists next door. Name them for the kind of maker, which is what the two plans really separate:

- **Hobby**, $10 a month. In my model: 150 Expert messages a month, Basic free. In yours: 750 credits.
- **Workshop**, $20 a month. In my model: 350 Expert messages a month. In yours: 1,000 credits plus unlimited Basic.

Both words are already in this audience's mouth, neither sounds like a software tier, and "Workshop" says heavy use without saying "unlimited".

**The pack.** Call the option **Pay as you go** and the thing you buy by its contents, "100 Expert messages, $10, never expire" or "500 credits". "Pack" and "bundle" sound like a one-time starter; "pay as you go" says what it is, and it is the phrase your own draft reached for. The reload toggle is "Auto-reload", your word, with its discount stated beside it.

**The free first month.** "Your first month: 100 Expert messages on us." Not "trial", which promises a wall at the end, and not "welcome coins", which needs the mapping line again.

36

38

40	
41	Where: the balance breakdown, Preferences › Account, and one notice.
42

44	
45	### 5. The next message costs more than the person has
46	
47	Where: the composer, before sending; the failed-message card if the gateway refuses anyway.
48	
49	This is the boundary where every surveyed product earns its anger. Opinion: catch it before sending. The app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next Expert message cannot be paid, the Send button becomes "Send with Basic (1 coin)" and a one-line note says why: "You have 3 credits; Expert needs 5." The typed text is untouched. "Buy credits" and "Subscribe" sit next to it, not instead of it. Only a race between two sends reaches the gateway's 402, and the failed card then does the same three things with the text kept in the composer.
50	
51	Earlier than that: when the balance falls below one session's worth of the chat's tier (about 25 credits for Expert), the composer says once "About 5 Expert messages left", so the boundary is expected, not met.
52	
53	### 6. Unlimited Basic and its ceiling
54	
55	Where: the plan page, Preferences › Account, one notice in the composer.
56	
57	Risk: "unlimited" that stops at 600 reads as a lie. Opinion: never write "unlimited" alone. 58	
59	### 7. Subscription credits the person did not use
60	
61	Where: Preferences › Account; one notice; the suggestion line.
62	
63	Kenneth expects most subscribers to use under half their credits. Opinion: tell them. The month-end notice is the same as point 4 ("240 credits expire on 30 Nov"). 64

66	
67	### 8. Buying
68	
69	Where: the pricing page in the browser (Chargebee hosted checkout), then back in the app.
70

72	
73	Back in the app: the balance refreshes when the window regains focus, and the composer shows one line, "+500 credits", so the person knows it worked without opening Preferences.
74	
75	### 9. When the welcome month ends
76	
77	Where: the first launch after day 30.
78	
79	Risk: the person comes back to zero and reads it as "the free trial is over, pay up", the moment Obico's data says people leave. 80

82	
83	Where: the G-code marker in the chat and the print history, after a print.
84	
85	Opinion: show the reward before the work, in the button itself: "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits". The form says what earns it: a photo of the printed object and a few sentences. 88

90	
91	Opinion: credits and prices appear only on the JusPrin provider's entries. A person with both an own key and an account sees "OpenAI · gpt-5.4-mini" without a price and "JusPrin · Expert · 5 credits" with one. Nothing about credits appears anywhere for a person who never signs in.
92	
93	### 12. Obico members
94	
95	Where: the pricing page and Preferences › Account.
96	
97	Opinion: one line, "Obico member: 20% off subscriptions", shown as the price on the card and as a note in Account. It is detected, never claimed or entered.

100	
101	Three boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas, in this order, because they carry the most risk: the composer with the tier label, balance and the pre-send "Send with Basic" state (points 2, 3, 5); Preferences › Account with the breakdown, the fair-use count and the activity list (points 3, 4, 6, 7); the pricing page's three cards (point 8).
